reference_title: UFC 4-023-03, Design of Buildings to Resist Progressive Collapse (DoD, dated 14 July 2009, as amended through Change 4, 10 June 2024)
scope_note: All 14 numbered/captioned figures in Chapter 3 (the Tie Force and Alternate Path design procedures), all 8 figures in Appendix B (structural-analysis definition diagrams: joint/connection rotation, yield/plastic rotation, panel zone, story drift), all 13 figures in Appendix C (commentary: tie-force justification diagrams, the printed Dynamic Increase Factor data-fit chart, and the steel connection-type illustrations supporting Table C-1), and the 4 building-geometry/tie-layout figures from Appendix D (the reinforced-concrete worked example this package validates against in tie_forces.py/enhanced_local_resistance.py). All 39 pages were located directly during full-document text extraction (each figure's own page marker was read alongside its caption) and independently cross-checked against this document's own front-matter List of Figures (printed pp. ix-xi) -- both sources agree at every entry; page_estimated=false throughout. Appendices E, F, and G (structural-steel/wood/cold-formed-steel worked-example figures: building plans, member-size call-outs, SAP2000 screenshots, hinge-property plots) are NOT cataloged -- narrow, software-workflow-specific content for one example building each, not general design figures of the kind this package catalogs elsewhere (see the package __init__.py docstring scope note).

figures.caption: Tie Forces in a Frame Structure
figures.description: Illustrates the three horizontal ties (longitudinal/transverse internal ties, dashed peripheral tie) and the vertical tie in a framed building, per Section 3-1's Tie Force method.

figures.caption: Sub-areas, Peripheral and Internal Ties for Non-uniform Floor Loads
figures.description: Shows how a floor plan with heavy- and light-load sub-areas is split, with a peripheral tie placed at the sub-area boundary sized to the sum of both sub-areas' peripheral tie strength (Section 3-1.3.2.2).

figures.caption: Determination of L1 and Column Area for Frame and Two-way Span Load-bearing Wall Construction
figures.description: Defines L1 (longitudinal/transverse bay spacing) and the column/wall strip (0.2*L wide) within which internal tie force may not exceed twice the required strength per unit length (Equation 3-3, Section 3-1.4.1.1).

figures.caption: Location Restrictions for Internal and Peripheral Ties that are Parallel to the Long Axis of a Beam, Girder or Spandrel
figures.description: Shows the exclusion zone directly above/within a beam, girder, or spandrel where internal and peripheral ties may not be placed unless the member can sustain a 0.20-rad rotation.

figures.caption: Determination of L1 and Column Area for One-way Load-bearing Wall Construction with hw = 12-ft (3.7-m)
figures.description: Defines L1 (LL longitudinal, LT=5*hw transverse) and the wall strip for one-way load-bearing wall construction (Equation 3-5, Section 3-1.4.1.2).

figures.caption: Splice Locations and Interruptions in Internal Tie Forces
figures.description: Shows the permitted 60%-of-bay-length splice zone (Section 3-1.6.1, ``tie_forces.splice_exclusion_zone``) and how internal ties are interrupted at openings/courtyards and anchored to peripheral ties with seismic hooks.

figures.caption: Definition of Force-Controlled and Deformation Controlled Actions, from ASCE 41
figures.description: The generalized force-deformation (Type 1/2/3) curve used by Section 3-2.5's classification rule (``alternate_path.classify_action``), with points a, b, c referenced throughout the material-chapter modeling-parameter tables.

figures.caption: Removal of Column from Alternate Path Model
figures.description: Shows beam-to-beam continuity assumed maintained across a removed column for Alternate Path analysis (Section 3-2.9).

figures.caption: Location of External Column Removal for RC II Option 2, RC III and IV Structures
figures.description: Plan showing the minimum external-column removal locations: mid-short-side, mid-long-side, and building corner (Section 3-2.9.2.2).

figures.caption: Location of Internal Column Removal for RC II Option 2, RC III and IV Structures
figures.description: Plan showing internal-column removal locations within areas of underground parking or uncontrolled public access (Section 3-2.9.2.3).

figures.caption: Location of External Load-Bearing Wall Removal for RC II Option 2, RC III and RC IV Structures
figures.description: Plan showing the minimum external-load-bearing-wall removal locations, including the corner condition removing a length H in each direction (Section 3-2.9.2.4).

figures.caption: Location of Internal Load-Bearing Wall Removal for RC II Option 2, RC III and RC IV Structures
figures.description: Plan showing internal-load-bearing-wall removal locations within areas of underground parking or uncontrolled public access (Section 3-2.9.2.5).

figures.caption: Loads and Load Locations for External and Internal Column Removal for Linear and Nonlinear Static Models (Left Side Demonstrates External Column Removal; Right Side Shows Internal Column Removal)
figures.description: Shows the increased-gravity-load region (bays A-B-C-D immediately above/adjacent to the removed column) vs. the rest of the structure, for Equations 3-10/3-12/3-15 (``alternate_path.deformation_controlled_load_lsp`` etc.).

figures.caption: Loads and Load Locations for External and Internal Wall Removal for Linear and Nonlinear Static Models (Left Side Demonstrates External Wall Removal; Right Side Shows Internal Wall Removal)
figures.description: The wall-removal counterpart to Figure 3-13, showing the increased-gravity-load region above/adjacent to a removed load-bearing wall section.

figures.caption: Joint and Connection Definition
figures.description: Distinguishes a 'joint' (the central region where members attach) from a 'connection' (the link transmitting actions between components), per ASCE 41 terminology used throughout the acceptance-criteria tables.

figures.caption: Joint and Connection Rotations
figures.description: Shows joint rotation Gamma (rigid-body rotation) vs. connection rotation theta, the deformation measure used in the m-factor and plastic-rotation acceptance tables.

figures.caption: Definition of Chord Rotation (from ASCE 41)
figures.description: Shows chord rotation as the practical means of computing connection rotation theta in a frame model.

figures.caption: Definition of Yield Rotation, Plastic Rotation, and Total Rotation
figures.description: Moment-rotation curve defining theta_y (yield rotation), theta_p (plastic rotation), and total rotation theta -- the quantities tabulated in Tables 4-1/4-3 (a, b modeling parameters) and referenced by Table 3-5's DIF rotation ratio.

figures.caption: Plastic Hinge and Rotation
figures.description: Shows a discrete plastic-hinge model inserted into a frame member, illustrating how numerical models typically ignore the small elastic joint rotation and model only the connection's plastic rotation.

figures.caption: Panel Zone
figures.description: Shows the steel-frame column-web panel zone (high shear stress region at a fully-restrained beam-to-column moment connection), per ASCE 41 Sections 9.5.2.2.1-9.5.2.2.2.

figures.caption: Story Drift
figures.description: Defines story drift (lateral deflection Delta over wall height h) as the nonlinear deformation measure for load-bearing-wall structures (masonry, wood, cold-formed steel).

figures.caption: Vertical Wall Deflection (Drift)
figures.description: Adapts the story-drift deformation measure (Figure B-7) to VERTICAL wall deflection caused by a removed wall section in progressive-collapse analysis, rather than horizontal seismic drift.

figures.caption: Damaged and Undamaged Structural Elements
figures.description: Shows how the floor system transfers vertical load from a removed-column panel region, through undamaged framing members, to the vertical load-carrying elements -- the physical basis for the Tie Force approach (Section C-5.3).

figures.caption: Column Removal Locations
figures.description: The six column-removal scenarios (corner, penultimate, internal, near-penultimate, edge, near-edge) analyzed in the Stevens 2008 study underlying the printed Tie Force equations.

figures.caption: Plan View of One-way Load-bearing Wall Structure
figures.description: Plan showing the four one-way load-bearing-wall removal locations analyzed to derive Equation 3-7 (end wall-center, end wall-end, interior wall-center, interior wall-end).

figures.caption: Loads in a One-way Load-bearing Wall Structure
figures.description: Idealized floor-load diagram (wall load, floor load, facade load) above a removed one-way load-bearing wall section, underlying Equation 3-7's WC/WW terms.

figures.caption: Tie Force in Upper Chord of Roof Joist
figures.description: Shows how the top chord of an open-web steel joist can supply the internal tie force for lightweight roof systems, per Section 3-1's roof-system guidance.

figures.caption: Tie Force in Steel Deck
figures.description: Shows how a transversely-spanning steel deck can supply the internal tie force across a joist line, with the deck's upper surface remaining intact after 0.20-rad rotation despite crushing at the joist.

figures.caption: Dynamic Increase Factor for Structural Steel
figures.description: The printed data-fit chart underlying Table 3-5's steel DIF equation (Omega_N = 1.08+0.76/(theta_pra/theta_y+0.83)), showing SAP2000 study data points for 3-story and 10-story column-removal cases against the recommended-equation curve; fully digitized in ``alternate_path.table_3_5_dynamic_increase_factor``.

figures.caption: Fully Restrained Moment Connections
figures.description: Seven-panel illustration of the Fully Restrained (FR) connection types listed in Table C-1 (WUF, Welded Flange Plates, Welded Cover-Plated Flanges, Bolted Flange Plates, Free Flange, Top/Bottom Haunch, Reduced Beam Section) -- spans printed pp. 112-113.

figures.caption: Partially Restrained Moment Connections or Shear Connections
figures.description: Four-panel illustration of Partially Restrained (PR) connection types from Table C-1 (bolted/riveted angle, double split tee, unstiffened end plate, simple shear tab).

figures.caption: Weak Axis Moment Connection or Shear Connection
figures.description: Two-panel illustration of a fully restrained vs. typical shear-only connection at a column's weak axis.

figures.caption: Kaiser Bolted Bracket(R) Fully Restrained Connection
figures.description: Proprietary FR moment connection with cast-steel haunch brackets bolted to the column flange; listed in Table C-1's connection-type inventory.

figures.caption: SidePlate(R) Fully Restrained Moment Connection
figures.description: Proprietary FR moment connection with full-depth side plates and fillet welds; m-factor/modeling-parameter formulas digitized in structural_steel.py Tables 5-1/5-2.

figures.caption: SlottedWeb(TM) Fully Restrained Connection
figures.description: Proprietary FR moment connection similar to WUF with extended web slots separating the beam flanges from the web near the connection; listed in Table C-1.

figures.caption: Concrete Building Elevation
figures.description: Elevation of the 7-story reinforced-concrete moment-frame office building used in Appendix D's Tie Force / Enhanced Local Resistance worked example, which this package's tests validate against directly.

figures.caption: Concrete Building Plan
figures.description: Plan of the Appendix D example building, showing the 227-ft x 97-ft footprint, 37.5-ft bays, office/storage/corridor bay assignments, and stair/elevator opening locations referenced in Table D-1/D-2.

figures.caption: Typical Layout of Internal Ties
figures.description: Diagram of the internal longitudinal/transverse tie-bar layout in an exterior bay of the Appendix D example, replacing the preliminary #3-at-12-inch slab reinforcement.

figures.caption: Typical Anchorage of Internal Ties to Peripheral Ties
figures.description: Shows the seismic-hook anchorage of internal ties into the peripheral tie within the 3-ft peripheral-tie width, per Section 3-1.6.1.
